chunks: And from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Allah, majestic is His remembrance, indeed created Laylat al-Qadr at the very beginning of creating the world, and in it He created the first Prophet who would be and the first Waṣī who would be. And He decreed that in every year there would be a night in which the explanation of affairs would descend until its like in the coming year.

Whoever denies that has rejected Allah’s knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, for the Prophets, the Messengers, and the Muḥaddathūn do not stand except that there is a proof upon them by what comes to them in that night together with the proof that Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) brings to them. I said: And do the Muḥaddathūn also receive Jibrāʾīl, or someone else from the angels (عليه السلام)? He said: As for the Prophets and the Messengers, blessings of Allah be upon them, there is no doubt; and it is necessary for those besides them, from the first day on which the earth was created until the end of the world’s annihilation, that there be a divine proof over the people of the earth, to whom that descends on that night from among whomever He loves of His servants.

By Allah, the Spirit and the angels indeed descended with the command on Laylat al-Qadr upon Ādam; and by Allah, Ādam did not die except that he had a Waṣī. And everyone after Ādam from among the Prophets received the command in it and assigned it to his Waṣī after him. And by Allah, the Prophet was indeed commanded regarding what came to him of the affair on that night, from Ādam to Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), that he should appoint so-and-so as successor.

And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has indeed said in His Book specifically concerning the possessors of authority after Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله): “Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the earth just as He made those before them successors” up to His saying, “then those are the defiantly disobedient.”

He says: I make you successors for My knowledge, My religion, and My worship after your Prophet, just as He made the successors of Ādam after him until He sends the Prophet who follows him: “They worship Me, not associating anything with Me.” He says: They worship Me with faith that there is no Prophet after Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله); so whoever says otherwise, then those are the defiantly disobedient.

So He has indeed established the possessors of authority after Muḥammad with knowledge, and we are they. So ask us; then if we speak truthfully to you, acknowledge it—though you will not do so. As for our knowledge, it is manifest; and as for the time of our appointed term in which the religion will appear through us until there remains no disagreement among people, it has a fixed term through the passage of nights and days. When it comes, it will appear and the affair will become one.

By Allah, the matter has indeed been decreed that there should be no disagreement among the believers. For that reason He made them witnesses over the people: so that Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) may be a witness over us, and that we may be witnesses over our Shīʿah, and that our Shīʿah may be witnesses over the people. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuses that there be difference in His judgment or contradiction among the people of His knowledge.

Then Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: The superiority of the believer’s faith in the statement “Indeed, We sent it down” and in its interpretation over one who is not like him in faith in it is like the superiority of the human being over beasts. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, indeed repels through the believers in it against those who deny it in this world, so as to complete the punishment of the Hereafter for those whom He knows will not repent from among them, just as He repels by the strivers against those who remain seated. And I do not know in this time any jihad except hajj, ʿumrah, and good neighborliness.

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: the opening Qur'anic phrase of Sūrat al-Qadr, central to the hadith’s teaching
key_terms.الْفَاسِقُونَ: those who defiantly depart from obedience
key_terms.الْمُحَدَّثُونَ: those who are spoken to or inspired, distinct from Prophets and Messengers
key_terms.تَفْسِيرِ الْأُمُورِ: the explanation and detailing of affairs decreed for the coming period
key_terms.حُجَّةٌ: a divinely established proof or authority over creation
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Decree in which divine affairs descend each year
key_terms.وَصِيٌّ: the designated successor appointed after a Prophet
key_terms.وُلَاةِ الْأَمْرِ: the possessors of authority after the Prophet

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain Laylat al-Qadr and its connection to the Imams after the Prophet Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This narration presents Laylat al-Qadr as a recurring divine event through which Allah conveys the unfolding of affairs and sustains His proof upon the earth through Prophets, Awṣiyāʾ, and the possessors of authority. It connects the interpretation of Sūrat al-Qadr with the doctrine of continuing divine authority after the Prophet Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), and affirms that true faith includes belief in both the revelation and its divinely designated interpreters.
